description: Translations for any .NET 10+ app, written in C# and checked at compile time: a class per language, inline texts, or an attribute on a type or its members. A missing translation, or one that never uses a value the original shows, is a build error. No resource files, no dependencies, safe to trim and to publish with Native AOT.
releaseNotes:
Every text is a string. ShopLocalization.Checkout, ShopLocalization.Greeting(customer.Name), LocalizableText.Inline(...), LocalizableText.GetTextByMember and GetText() each give the wording for the user's language at the moment you read them. Read a text where you show it, because a string kept in a static field stays in the language of the first user. The build warns about a text in the initializer of a static field or property (LOC602). LocalizableText is no longer a type you hold. It only has Inline, GetTextByMember and GetTextOfType. Its conversions, its equality, ToString(culture), Key, FullKey, Contract, Arguments, Keyed, GetWording and its JSON converter are gone. A parameter that took a LocalizableText takes a string. Rebuild every library built with an earlier version, because the generated code calls other methods.

A text takes a value as a method of its set. Write Greeting(string name) in each language and call ShopLocalization.Greeting(customer.Name). LocalizableText.Format is gone, and nothing fills in a placeholder such as {0} any more, so a wording that holds one shows its braces (LOC403, with an IDE fix that writes the method). Each language writes its own plurals in C#, because a wording can depend on its values.

A set can hold the texts of an enum. List ILocalizationSet<OrderStatus> in place of ILocalizationSet, and every member of the enum needs a text in every language (CS0535). order.Status.GetText() gives a value its text, and so does OrderStatusLocalization.GetTextByValue(order.Status). A value that two members have gives the text of the first, so OrderStatus.None.GetText() next to Default = 0 is a build warning (LOC600).

A label can sit on the member it names. Mark a property, a field, an enum member or a type [Localized(en: "City", nl: "Plaats")], with a wording per language. LocalizableText.GetTextByMember<Address>(nameof(Address.City)) gives the text, also by a Type or a PropertyInfo your code holds. LocalizableText.GetTextOfType<Address>() gives the text of a type itself, and a value of an enum gives the text of its member with GetText(). The source generator writes each text as code, so nothing reads the attribute at run time. A member of an enum without [Localized] next to members that have it is a build warning (LOC501), and so is GetText() on the later of two marked members with one value (LOC600).

The build holds every language to the values. A language whose method never uses a value the default wording shows doesn't build (LOC402), and neither does a language of LocalizableText.Inline that leaves out a value the default language shows.

The names say localization. A set implements ILocalizationSet and its contract: class ShopLocalizationNl : ILocalizationSet, IShopLocalization. The registry is LocalizationRegistry, and [ExcludeFromLocalizationDiscovery] keeps a set or a member out. A set's name ends in its language in PascalCase, such as ShopLocalizationEnGb for en-GB, and an inline text takes enGb: for it. A class that lists only a contract is no set. A set states its language in LocalizationLanguageCode, which was LanguageCode: string ILocalizationSet.LocalizationLanguageCode => "en-GB".

ResourceText is gone. The key of a text of a set is its name, such as Checkout. Every generated class has a method GetTextByKey, for a key your code only has at run time. ShopLocalization.GetTextByKey("Checkout") gives the wording, and GetTextByKey("Greeting", customer.Name) that of a text with parameters. A key no text has throws. No text can be named GetTextByKey any more (LOC300).

LocalizationRegistry.Create is gone, because nothing public read a text from a registry of your own. Read a set of your app with LocalizationRegistry.Current.Find. [Localized] written through an alias is a build warning (LOC502), and the fix for parameter names (LOC401) no longer moves names over parameters of different types.

LocalizationRegistry.CurrentUICultureProvider gives the user's culture in an app that keeps it somewhere other than CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture. LocalizationRegistry.UseCulture(culture) makes every text in a using block follow another culture, such as that of an email's recipient, also across an await.

An app declares its languages with [assembly: SupportedLanguages], also an app without texts of its own, such as a test project or the server project of a Blazor Web App. An app without the attribute doesn't build (LOC103). The languages of an app it references no longer count.

The codes of the build's messages have new numbers, grouped by subject, from LOC100 to LOC701. Update every code in a NoWarn or a #pragma. The page docs/build-errors.md lists each one, and marks those with an IDE fix.

A language code that no user's culture matches is a build warning (LOC104), such as dk for Danish, which is da, or en-UK, which is en-GB. The set of your default language can list ILocalizationSet through an abstract class it derives from. A set whose constructor reads a text of its own contract throws an InvalidOperationException that names the set, where the app stopped before. LOC600 is reported in Razor markup too.

The details have a page per subject under docs/, which the README links to. New is a page on performance, with measurements next to IStringLocalizer.
